title: TWICE AS MUCH ON THE SIXTH DAY

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'On the sixth day they are to prepare what they bring in, and that is to be
twice as much as they gather on the other days.'" - Ex 16:5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Before Israel has gathered a single flake, God is already planning their rest.

Notice the order of events. The Sabbath command has not yet been given at Sinai.
That comes later, in chapter 20. But God builds rest into the manna arrangement
from the very first week. Rest was not an afterthought bolted on to the law; it
was woven into how God fed His people from the start.

And notice the mercy in the arrangement. If they were to rest on the seventh
day, they would need food for it. So God provides double on the sixth. He never
commands rest without making rest possible.

That is a good thing to remember when we tell ourselves we cannot afford to
stop. Sometimes that is genuinely true for a season. But often our restlessness
comes from not believing God can provide for the day we are not working.

Rest is an act of trust. It says: the world will keep turning without me,
because it was never turning on me.

Jesus said the Sabbath was made for people, not people for the Sabbath (Mark
2:27). It was given as a gift before it was ever given as a rule.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you build rest into your week, or only collapse when exhausted?
2. What are you afraid will fall apart if you stop?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You that You provide for the days I rest as well as the days I work.
Help me to stop, and to trust You while I do. Amen.
